why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 2, 4 and 6 stay within their expect lines. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition says "the missing-file runs exit 2", and that includes `node $BIN missing.jsonl bad.jsonl`. In that run one file can't be read and the other has bad rows. Expect line 3 gives exit 2 for an unreadable file and exit 1 for a bad row, but it doesn't say which code wins when both happen. So requiring exit 2 is stricter than the words. The brief's own Advisory even lists this exact case ("Check whether exit status is 2 when one file is unreadable and another has bad rows") as not pass/fail, yet Check 3's PASS condition still enforces it. Check 5's "they pass" may also go slightly past its words. The Check 3 precedence rule alone means the criterion fails.
